map.summary: This area is the web front door of an evidence-backed document search product. Through their browser, a person picks a demo identity and collection, asks a question, and watches the answer arrive live with citations they can open and download the original source. All backend calls travel through the same website origin, which quietly rewrites paths, strips cookies, and streams results back.
unknowns: The forwarding destination is read from an environment setting; how that setting is populated in any deployed environment is not shown.
Only the frontend area was examined, so the shape of upstream responses and error payloads is taken on trust from this side.
The upload flow is described as reachable with accepted file types and a size limit, but the path from chosen file to stored document is not shown in these findings.
Direct-link parameters for workspace, answer, and source are honored, but how those links are generated for sharing is not shown.

diagrams.title: How a question becomes a cited answer
diagrams.description: A person picks a collection and identity, asks a question, and watches the answer stream back live. Citations can be opened to view and download the original source document.

diagrams.title: How requests are filtered and forwarded
diagrams.description: A browser request reaches the site forwarder, which rejects anything outside the allowed path shape, strips sensitive headers, and forwards the rest to the internal backend while streaming the reply back.

diagrams.title: Stopping or losing a connection
diagrams.description: If a person stops an answer or the connection drops, the site cancels the upstream request, clears the partial draft and citations, and shows a safe message rather than an invented answer.

diagrams.title: How a person switches identity
diagrams.description: Changing the simulated demo identity reloads workspace, collection, and capability choices, clears saved answers, open sources, and manager controls, and shows a read-only notice for view-only identities.

F0001.statement: The web app exposes a catch-all API route handler (forward, exported as GET/POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE) under /api/[...path] that acts as a fixed reverse proxy: it only permits paths whose first segment is "v1" and whose segments match /^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$/, returning a 404 not_found JSON error otherwise.

F0002.statement: The proxy builds its upstream URL from process.env.API_INTERNAL_URL (defaulting to http://127.0.0.1:8000) plus the sanitized path, and forwards request.method, selected headers, and the request body (with duplex: "half" for non-GET/HEAD methods), so browser clients reach the backend API through the same origin.

F0003.statement: Only an allowlist of request headers is forwarded upstream — content-type, accept, x-demo-user-id, idempotency-key, last-event-id — so cookies and authorization headers are intentionally stripped (the backend, not this proxy, owns authorization).

F0004.statement: The proxy streams upstream responses rather than buffering: it pipes response.body through a ReadableStream reader, forwards content-type, content-disposition, and x-request-id, and always sets Cache-Control: no-store and X-Accel-Buffering: no, which supports live server-sent-event answer streams.

F0005.statement: Cancellation is propagated end-to-end: the incoming request.signal is linked to a local AbortController that aborts the upstream fetch, and cancelling the downstream ReadableStream (cancel handler) or a read error aborts the upstream request and releases the reader.

F0006.statement: If the upstream fetch throws (e.g., connection refused), the proxy returns a sanitized 503 api_unavailable JSON error message and does not leak upstream error detail to the client.

F0007.statement: The home page (Home in page.tsx, exercised by page.test.tsx) is a client-side document workspace that loads demo identities, workspaces/collections, capabilities, documents, and saved answers from the same-origin API and renders selectors for collection scope and demo user identity.

F0008.statement: Asking a question streams answer events (progress, content, citations, complete, error) from the /answers/stream endpoint; partial "content" drafts are shown while streaming and are replaced by the final AnswerResult text once a "complete" event arrives.

F0009.statement: Failed or interrupted answer streams clear the in-progress draft and surface a safe message (e.g., "Connection interrupted" or the server-provided message such as "The answer could not be verified."); a new request is only started on explicit manual retry ("Retry question"), not automatically.

F0010.statement: While an answer is streaming the UI offers a "Stop" action that aborts the in-flight stream request (the fetch signal is marked aborted) and clears both the draft and any citations, showing "You stopped this answer" instead.

F0011.statement: Selecting a citation ("Open source 1") fetches and displays the currently authorized source document including original filename, page/locator info (e.g., "Page 2"), the cited passage text, and a "Download original" control.

F0012.statement: Switching the simulated demo identity reloads workspace/collection/capability data for the new identity and explicitly clears previously loaded answers, open source context (e.g., notes.txt), and manager-only controls like "Permissions"; a read-only identity instead sees a read-only notice about the collection.

F0013.statement: The page honors direct-link query parameters (workspace, answer, source) on load, using them to load the saved answer and open the referenced source through the selected identity, and preserves an explicit "All accessible collections" scope (collection_id null in the request body) across an answer refresh.

F0014.statement: The document workspace exposes an upload flow reachable from an "Add your documents" action, showing a "Choose a file" control and stated accepted inputs ("PDF, plain text, Markdown, or HTML · up to 20 MB").

F0015.statement: The root layout (RootLayout) wraps all pages with global styles, page metadata (title "Hybrid RAG Search" and a search-over-documents description), and a "Skip to content" accessibility link to #main-content.

F0016.statement: The Next.js configuration enables React strict mode and disables dev indicators and agent rules; next-env.d.ts only references Next's ambient types and generated route/param types, and is explicitly marked as not to be edited.
